clue.text: Boatman's a little troubled in the head

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter, so take the opening letters of the stretch after the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being slightly unwell, a bit muddled in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of "Boatman's" starts the run: the heads of S, A, LITTLE, TROUBLED give the letters. The setter's own pseudonym does double service as a plain word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, so a boatman in general terms.

clue.text: Missionary writer's last upset!

indicators.note: the tail of the word upset, read on its own, says set or arrange the letters before it afresh

explanation.surface: An exclamation of distress at the final lines of some author.
explanation.walkthrough: The final word must be split in two: its first half is fodder and its second half is the anagram signal; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul of Tarsus travelled spreading Christianity and wrote many New Testament epistles.

clue.text: Trees being planted in copses isn't unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A remark that it is common to find saplings put in among small woods.
explanation.definitionFit: This pine species native to northern Europe is a familiar conifer, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Look: dead drunk!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the four letters of dead stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone points out a person who has passed out from drink.
explanation.walkthrough: "drunk" is both the anagram signal for DEAD and, with the whole clue, the sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for heavily intoxicated, the state of the dead-drunk figure in view.

clue.text: Soak embraces tender beauty; it is so

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to seep is to soak through or ooze
a tender person is kind

explanation.surface: Someone drenched is hugging a gentle beauty, and that's the way it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying that beauty is only skin-deep: the answer is what beauty "is".
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that beauty is superficial, going no further than the surface of the skin.

clue.text: See 9
College head to hang around school corridor?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
around means the loitering surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to hang about is to loiter

explanation.surface: A college principal is told to hang around the school.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a cloister is a covered walkway, a kind of corridor round a quadrangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered arcade running round a courtyard, a passage like a corridor.

clue.text: Drink lots of stuff got from the Internet

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
loads means a great many, lots

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a great deal of material taken off the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Files pulled onto a computer from the web are the things one has fetched online.

clue.text: Wrong way to pass port wines? Cocktail shaker

indicators.note: a cocktail shaker jumbles its contents, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Passing port in the wrong direction, and wines in a cocktail shaker.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cocktail shaker" reads as a bar tool, but COCKTAIL is fodder and "shaker" the anagram signal. Port is traditionally passed to the left, that is clockwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining etiquette passes port clockwise to the left, so the opposite rotation is the wrong direction.

clue.text: Home in north Italy? Sad if Boatman's after it

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: the setter's word placed after the remaining piece completes the word for sad, so it is taken away

parts.note: gloomy means sad
the setter's possessive is my

explanation.surface: A dwelling in northern Italy, and the setter is grumpy if he goes after it.
explanation.walkthrough: The piece wanted is the one which, followed by MY ("Boatman's"), makes GLOOMY (sad), so the clue spells out GLOOMY with MY removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit snow-block shelters are the traditional dwelling of the Arctic north.

clue.text: A drink as drunk by an under-age person

indicators.note: something drunk by a person is taken inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A drink being consumed by a minor, which sounds like trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: "drunk" looks like an anagram signal, but with "by" it means swallowed, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a drink raised in someone's honour, so a drink in that ceremonial sense.

clue.text: Rural clockmaker to add online distribution

indicators.note: distribution spreads things around, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A country horologist decides to sell his clocks over the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Children tell the time by blowing the seeds from a dandelion's fluffy seed head, called a dandelion clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The weed's seed head is called a clock, so the plant of the countryside makes clocks.

clue.text: Under-age person, into whom I ply cocktail, leaves floating

indicators.note: into whom places the mixed letters inside the boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a young person
taken as written

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster being plied with mixed drinks, while foliage drifts on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-lily pads are the broad leaves that float on a pond's surface.

clue.text: See 8
Case's close: winner is he who gets repossession

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: In a court case's conclusion, the winner is the party who gets property back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who expels a tenant takes the property back, so repossession goes to this person.

clue.text: Starter prepared by roasting it

indicators.note: food prepared is made ready, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A first course made by roasting it.
explanation.walkthrough: "Starter" suggests a first course, given the roasting, but it means someone who starts things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instigates is the one who sets something going, a starter of trouble.

clue.text: Royal booze-up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lager is beer, booze

explanation.surface: A party for monarchs where the drink flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly or queenly, belonging to a monarch.

clue.text: Property crime re-appears once concealed

indicators.note: concealed means kept out of sight, here within the letters of other words

explanation.surface: An offence against property that turns up again having been covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to a building is a crime against property.

clue.text: Picture a drunk taking a snooze: quiet, please!

indicators.note: taking means the drunkard takes in the next pieces

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
a nap is a snooze
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Picture a drunkard dozing off, so please keep the noise down.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a casual photograph, a picture taken quickly.

clue.text: Bartender takes a pee: it's where we get beer

indicators.note: read Bartender as Bart-ender: its ender is its final letter

parts.note: pee is how the letter P is said

explanation.surface: The barman nips off to the toilet; that is where we get our beer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bartender" is split into BART and "ender", the last letter of BART; then A, then P.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer is drawn from a tap at the bar.

clue.text: Where throat may be swollen and dry, shot resettles one inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the rearranged letters
resettles means settles anew, so the letters are placed in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Where a sore throat swells and is dry, a jab settles one down.
explanation.walkthrough: "shot" looks like an injection, but it is anagram fodder with DRY, and "resettles" is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid gland sits in the neck and swells into a goitre at the throat.

clue.text: Child crushed grasshopper — no playful seraph

indicators.note: crushed means squashed out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no says the letters of the angel are subtracted from the insect
playful says the angel's letters come out in any order

explanation.surface: A child has stepped on an insect, a far from playful little angel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, E, R, A, P, H ("no playful seraph") from GRASSHOPPER, leaving G, S, O, P, R, and "crushed" shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a small child or baby.

clue.text: Dissident asks agent about Russian master

indicators.note: about means the agent goes round the other letters

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: a dissident breaks from the established order, so the letters break their order

explanation.surface: A Soviet dissident questions an agent about a Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Spassky was the Soviet world chess champion beaten by Bobby Fischer in 1972. "Dissident" looks like a noun but is the anagram signal for ASKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spassky was a Russian chess grandmaster and former world champion.

clue.text: Cocktail swallowed in evil excess of drink

indicators.note: swallowed in means taken inside another word

parts.note: sinful means wicked, evil

indicators.note: read Cocktail as cock-tail: the tail of the first part is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cocktail gulped down in a wicked binge of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cocktail" is split into COCK and "tail": its last letter K goes inside SINFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is as much alcohol as one can hold, enough to be drunk.

clue.text: Shah's man in Sparta murdered

indicators.note: murdered means destroyed, so the letters are ruined and remade

explanation.surface: The Persian king's envoy is killed in the Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor under the old Persian kings, ruling for the monarch.

clue.text: Bearing down on foot, first turn to wind before leading yachtsman

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: to luff is a sailing term for steering into the wind

indicators.note: leading means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A sailor bearing down on foot, making a first turn into the wind ahead of the lead yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bearing down" is not pressing hard but having soft feathers: carrying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in soft feathers or fuzz is fluffy, so it carries down.

clue.text: Drained whisky: a girl not to trust, having lost bottle opener

parts.note: Whisky is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
she stands for a girl or woman

indicators.note: having lost says a letter is removed from the doubting word

parts.note: to doubt is not to trust

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drained whisky, and a girl who can't be trusted after losing her nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: "bottle" in the surface is British slang for courage, but its first letter B is what DOUBT loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Washed-out describes someone pale and exhausted, drained of colour or energy.

clue.text: It's common for a drunk to lose everything

parts.note: losing everything is read as winning nothing, giving win
the nothing that is won is O, zero

explanation.surface: Losing everything is a familiar fate for an alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing everything is turned round into winning nothing, nought being written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Wino is a common slang word for an alcoholic, especially a vagrant drinker.

clue.text: To decapitate, remove head always

indicators.note: remove head means the first letter comes off

parts.note: to decapitate is to sever the head

explanation.surface: Instructions to behead: always take off the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, always, as in ever-ready.

clue.text: Dirt sticks to one with no self-control

indicators.note: sticks to puts the dirt beside the single item

parts.note: a means one
muck is dirt

explanation.surface: Grime clings to someone who can't control himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok, or amuck, means behaving wildly and out of control.

clue.text: A bunch maybe control space?

definitions.meaning: a bunch carried on a ring for locks, of the sort that open doors
Control and Space are examples of buttons on a computer board

explanation.surface: A bunch, perhaps, that keeps order in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Keys come in bunches for opening locks, and Control and Space are keyboard buttons.

clue.text: Someone driving me out, playing snare

indicators.note: driving ... out says the letters of me are expelled from the other word
out completes driving out, signalling removal of letters
playing means the letters left over are toyed with into new order

explanation.surface: Someone forcing me out by playing a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMEONE without M and E ("driving me out") leaves S, O, O, N, E, which "playing" rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a running loop that tightens, a snare for catching animals.

clue.text: No drink in the pot for Spooner's former nymph?

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a flagon is a large drinking vessel or pot
dry means without drink

explanation.surface: An empty pot, as the famously tongue-tied Dr Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: "Flagon dry" (no drink in the pot) with first sounds swapped becomes DRAGON FLY. The adult insect develops from a water nymph, hence "former nymph".
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly grows from an aquatic nymph, so it was formerly a nymph.
